Nine Dead In Erie Shooting; Police Reveal Family Connection
sources.text:
Nine people are dead, including the suspected shooter, after a mass shooting at a home in Erie, Pennsylvania, with police revealing Saturday that seven of the eight victims were related to the gunman.
Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah said the suspected shooter was a 45-year-old man and that the eighth victim was a friend of a pregnant woman killed in the attack, The Associated Press reported.
Two young children were also among the dead. Authorities have not publicly identified those killed or announced a motive.
Two Women Arrived Before Shooting
Investigators recovered video and audio evidence showing two “distressed” women arriving at the home shortly before 5 p.m. Friday and pounding on the door, according to Lorah.
The gunman then came outside and shot the women before returning inside, AP reported.
Police arrived to find the two women dead outside the residence.
Inside the home, officers found a 5-year-old boy, a 1-year-old girl, two additional women, two young men, and the suspected shooter, according to AP.
One of the adult victims was pregnant.
The total of nine dead includes the suspected shooter, meaning eight people were killed by the gunman. AP corrected its developing coverage Saturday to make that distinction clear.
Police Correct Early Standoff Reports
The City of Erie said officers arrived “within minutes” after receiving a ShotSpotter alert.
Early reports described an extended standoff and suggested additional gunfire occurred after officers reached the home. The city later said investigators determined all nine people were already dead before police arrived.
“The deaths were not the result of any prolonged standoff or delay in police action,” the city said.
Police also determined no additional gunshots were fired after officers arrived. Sounds that may have been mistaken for gunfire were flash-bang devices deployed as part of the tactical response, according to the city.
Officers initially had limited information about whether the shooter remained alive inside the home or continued to pose a threat. Police assessed the situation and gathered information while seeking a search warrant.
Investigators Search For Motive
Police have not announced what led to the killings.
Lorah said investigators plan to interview other relatives and examine the cellphones of the women found outside the home as they reconstruct the events preceding the shooting.
Lorah described the crime scene as unprecedented during his law enforcement career.
“They knew something was going on at that house,” Lorah said, reported AP. “I have not seen anything like this in my 28-plus years,”
Authorities have not publicly released the identities of the victims or shooter.
Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro said he had spoken with Erie Mayor Daria Devlin and offered the city his administration’s full support.
What Remains Unknown
Investigators have not announced a motive or publicly explained what prompted the two women to rush to the house shortly before they were killed.
Authorities also have not released the victims’ names.
Although additional details circulated following Saturday’s police briefing, the investigation remains active, and some information reported during the first hours after the shooting changed as detectives reconstructed the timeline.
The City of Erie specifically urged residents to avoid spreading unverified information while investigators worked to establish the facts.
Previous Mass Shootings Covered By DX
The Erie deaths follow other mass-casualty shootings covered this year by The Dallas Express.
In April, The Dallas Express reported that eight children were killed and two women hospitalized in a shooting in Shreveport, Louisiana. Police identified Shamar Elkins as the suspect and later killed him following a vehicle pursuit and shootout.
In March, The Dallas Express covered a shooting at Buford’s on Sixth Street in Austin that killed two victims and wounded 14 before responding officers fatally shot the gunman. Another wounded victim later died, The Dallas Express subsequently reported.
The Erie investigation remains active as detectives work to determine what prompted the shooting and what the two women knew when they arrived at the home.

sources.news_title: Children, pregnant woman among 9 dead in Pennsylvania shooting
Gunman kills pregnant woman, 2 children and 5 others in ‘devastating’ Pennsylvania rampage
Nine killed in Pennsylvania mass shooting, motive yet to be established
sources.text:
A 45-year-old man shot and killed eight people, including a pregnant woman and two children, then apparently shot himself to death in Erie, Pennsylvania, authorities said on Saturday at a press conference where they revealed details of the previous evening's shooting.
The shooter, who has yet to be identified, died of an apparent self-inflicted wound before officers arrived on the scene, said Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah.
"Some scenes stay with you long after you leave them. This is one of those tragic scenes," Lorah said.
Eight victims were family members, police say
Police have yet to establish a motive, Lorah said. He said eight of the nine who died in the shooting were family members, and one was a family friend.
Lorah said after the shooter entered the home, he came out of the house and shot two women who appeared "distressed" and were pacing back and forth seeking assistance from neighbors.
Police found the suspect on the second floor of the home on Perry Street, Lorah said.
Erie Mayor Daria Devlin said the police department "arrived at a horrific scene, faced unimaginable circumstances, and carried out their duties with courage and professionalism."
"They too are members of this community, and they too will carry the weight of what happened last night," she said.
Earlier, Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro said in a statement on X/Twitter that he had spoken with Mayor Devlin and had offered support following "the tragic mass shooting."

NEW YORK (VINnews) — A shooting in a residential neighborhood of Erie, Pennsylvania, left nine people dead, including the suspected gunman, on Friday, in what the city’s police chief described as one of the most devastating scenes of his nearly three-decade career.

The shooting occurred near East Seventh and Perry streets on the city’s East Side. Authorities have not released the identities of the victims or established a motive for the attack. Two children were among the dead, according to local media reports.
Police Chief Rick Lorah described the circumstances as “deeply disturbing” and said he had never witnessed anything comparable in his more than 28 years in law enforcement.
“I’m not sure that the city of Erie has ever seen the loss of life and the devastation that we just witnessed,” Lorah told a local news station.
According to the city of Erie, officers were dispatched after receiving an alert from ShotSpotter, a gunshot-detection system that uses a network of microphones and automated analysis to identify possible gunfire. Police arrived within minutes, officials said. Investigators subsequently determined that all nine deaths had occurred before officers reached the scene.
The city issued a statement Saturday to correct what it described as inaccurate information circulating after the shooting. It stressed that the deaths were not caused by a prolonged police standoff or a delay in the emergency response.
Officials also clarified that no additional gunshots were fired after officers arrived. Sounds that residents may have mistaken for gunfire during the police operation were flash-bang devices used by tactical officers, the statement said.
Local media reported that two women were found dead outside the residence, while additional victims were discovered inside. The suspected gunman also died, reportedly from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, according to police statements reported by ABC News and other outlets.
Authorities have not yet disclosed the suspect’s identity, his relationship to the victims or what may have prompted the violence.
Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro said Saturday that he had spoken with Erie Mayor Daria Devlin and offered the full support of his administration following the tragedy.
“I’ve spoken with Mayor Devlin and offered my Administration’s full support following the tragic mass shooting in Erie last night,” Shapiro wrote in a social media post.
The city also expressed condolences to the victims’ families and urged residents to avoid spreading unverified claims. Officials warned that inaccurate information could increase the distress of grieving families, cause unnecessary fear and potentially interfere with public safety. A news conference was scheduled for Saturday afternoon, when authorities were expected to provide further details about the investigation.
The investigation remains ongoing, with key questions, including the suspect’s motive and the circumstances surrounding the victims’ deaths, still unanswered.

—Where. 722 Perry Street, near East 7th and Perry streets, on the East Side of Erie, Pennsylvania.
—When. Friday 9 October 2026, at about 5 p.m. Eastern time.

Officers went to the scene after a ShotSpotter alert, a system that uses sensors to detect gunfire and tell police where it came from. Police dispatch was at about 4:50 p.m., and officers arrived within minutes.
Two women were found dead on the sidewalk and street outside the home. Police and SWAT officers, a specially trained tactical team, then surrounded the house and obtained a search warrant.
When officers entered, they found more victims dead inside, including at least two children. In total, eight victims and the suspected gunman died.
Police say all of the deaths happened before officers arrived. No shots were fired after police got there, and the loud bangs heard nearby were police flash-bang devices, which make a loud noise and bright flash to disorient people.

sources.news_title: 9 people dead in mass shooting in Erie, Pa., including 2 children
Eight Victims, Including Children, Killed in Pennsylvania Mass Shooting as Suspected Gunman Dies at Erie Home
sources.text:
Nine people, including the suspected attacker, were found dead after gunfire erupted inside and outside a residence in Erie, Pennsylvania, prompting an armed police response and an investigation into one of the city’s deadliest acts of violence.
By yourNEWS Media Newsroom
ERIE, Pa. — Eight people, including children, were killed in a shooting at a home in Erie on Friday, Oct. 9, before the suspected gunman apparently took his own life, authorities said Saturday. Police discovered victims inside and outside the residence following reports of gunfire, prompting a response by tactical officers as investigators worked to establish what led to the killings.
The violence unfolded shortly before 5 p.m. in a residential neighborhood near East Seventh and Perry streets, where witnesses reported seeing an armed individual firing shots before entering a house. Officers arriving at the location discovered two women who had been fatally shot outside the property, while additional victims remained inside.
The initial reports from Erie police and local television stations described nine fatalities in total, including the suspected shooter, who reportedly died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound. Authorities subsequently confirmed that children were among those killed, although the identities of the victims and their relationships to one another had not been publicly established.
Police Chief Rick Lorah characterized the scene as among the most difficult he had encountered in more than 28 years of law enforcement. Investigators were still examining evidence at the property and interviewing witnesses Saturday, with officials declining to speculate about a possible motive.
“I want to be candid with our community. This is one of the most difficult and heartbreaking scenes our officers and investigators have ever encountered. The loss of life is devastating, and the circumstances we are working through are deeply disturbing,” Lorah said.
Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro responded Saturday morning by offering state assistance to Erie authorities and expressing condolences to the families affected. The governor said he had spoken with Erie Mayor Daria Devlin following the shootings and pledged support for the city’s response and investigation.
“I’ve spoken with Mayor Devlin and offered my Administration’s full support following the tragic mass shooting in Erie last night — killing nine of our fellow Pennsylvanians,” Shapiro wrote.
“My heart breaks for this family. Lori and I are praying for their loved ones and the entire Erie community,” he concluded.
The Erie Police Department said officers were initially alerted to the gunfire through ShotSpotter, an automated acoustic detection system designed to identify sounds consistent with gunshots and notify nearby law enforcement agencies. Additional reports from witnesses helped direct responding personnel to the residence.
According to the department’s official account of the emergency response, the shooting had stopped before officers arrived. Police emphasized that no additional gunfire occurred after the first responding units reached the location, seeking to clarify accounts of loud noises heard during the subsequent tactical operation.
The distinction became important as the response developed into an operation involving the Erie Police Department’s Special Weapons and Tactics team. Officers surrounded the residence while attempting to determine whether the person believed responsible remained armed and whether anyone inside might still be alive.
Authorities obtained a search warrant before tactical officers entered the home. During the operation, officers used flashbang devices, which create loud explosive sounds and flashes of light to disorient potential threats. Police said some noises that residents interpreted as additional gunfire were associated with the tactical response rather than continued shooting.
Once officers secured the residence, investigators discovered additional victims and the suspected attacker. Police believe the gunman died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound, although the circumstances of his death remained subject to the investigation.
The emergency response drew numerous police vehicles, tactical personnel and other first responders to the neighborhood. Officers restricted access to the surrounding streets while investigators documented evidence, examined the location of the victims and worked to reconstruct the sequence of events.
Lorah told local television station WFXP that the scale of the loss of life was unlike anything he had previously encountered during his career.
“It’s a horrific scene,” Lorah said. “There was a large loss of life inside that residence and outside that residence. … I can tell you that this is a tragic, tragic situation.”
The chief acknowledged that investigators still had substantial work ahead of them, particularly in determining the attacker’s motive and the circumstances connecting the people found at the property.
Authorities had not released the suspect’s name or publicly identified the victims as of Saturday’s initial reports. Investigators also had not established whether the shooting stemmed from a domestic dispute, another personal conflict or circumstances unrelated to the relationships among those involved.
Officials were seeking to notify relatives before releasing additional identifying information, while investigators continued reviewing physical evidence and statements from people who witnessed portions of the attack.
The discovery of multiple victims inside a private residence distinguishes the Erie killings from other recent mass shootings that occurred in public settings. In July, a shooting at Seattle Center in Washington left three people dead and several others wounded, with investigators examining evidence that multiple armed individuals had exchanged gunfire. That incident was unrelated to the Erie killings.
Authorities have also investigated shootings at public gatherings elsewhere in the country, including gunfire near a festival in Toledo, Ohio, where police pursued a suspect after multiple people were shot. Investigators have reported no connection between those incidents and Friday’s attack in Pennsylvania.
In Erie, investigators were concentrating on events at the residence and the identity and actions of the suspected shooter. The department’s Criminal Investigations Division remained responsible for examining the killings, including the collection of forensic evidence and the review of witness accounts.
Lorah said the investigation would require time because of the number of victims and the circumstances inside the property. He declined to provide additional details that could interfere with establishing the sequence of events or notifying surviving family members.
The City of Erie issued a public statement Friday night confirming multiple deaths and emphasizing that police had contained the incident. Officials said the suspected shooter was dead and that investigators had found no evidence of an additional threat to residents.
“We understand that this news brings deep shock and sorrow to our residents, and we want to assure the public that the situation has been contained,” the city said.
“Our thoughts are with the victims, their loved ones, and everyone impacted by tonight’s tragedy,” the statement continued. “We will continue working closely with our Erie Police Dept, and will provide updates as soon as verified information becomes available.”
The city’s announcement sought to reassure residents who had watched police surround the house and heard reports of gunfire during the emergency operation. Officials urged the public to rely on information released by law enforcement as investigators worked to verify the circumstances.
Erie, a city of approximately 90,000 residents along Lake Erie in northwestern Pennsylvania, lies roughly 120 miles north of Pittsburgh. The deaths have prompted condolences from local and state leaders, who have emphasized assistance for the victims’ relatives and the first responders involved.
The presence of children among those killed has added to the impact of the shooting, although authorities have not yet provided a complete breakdown of the victims’ ages. Investigators were expected to release further details after relatives were notified and the preliminary examination of the scene was completed.
The investigation also involves determining precisely when each victim was shot and whether any additional circumstances preceded the violence. Police have not publicly identified a surviving suspect or suggested that a second attacker was involved.
Lorah said the department would provide additional information once investigators had established facts that could be released without compromising their work. An update was expected Saturday as police continued processing the residence and coordinating with other authorities.
The deaths have left the Erie community awaiting answers about why the attack occurred and how the suspected gunman came to kill multiple people at the property. For now, authorities have confirmed nine fatalities, including the suspected shooter, and have said there is no continuing danger to the public.
The investigation remains active as police work to identify every victim, establish the relationships among those involved and determine the circumstances behind Friday’s killings.

Separately, US President Donald Trump on Friday (local time) described the death penalty as "a very worthy way" of executing former US Army Major Nidal Hasan, convicted of killing 13 people in the 2009 mass shooting at Fort Hood, Texas, saying he did not care how the convicted shooter was executed as long as he was put to death.
When asked whether he wanted Hasan's execution to be live-streamed and whether he was concerned that the video could be used as propaganda to radicalise others, Trump said the decision would be made by the authorities but confirmed that Hasan would be executed by firing squad.
"Well, they'll make a determination about that, but he will be killed. He will be, by firing squad. He killed 13, 14 people, badly wounded 20-some-odd people, and he's totally nuts. So, I really don't care how he goes, as long as he goes. And I think that the death penalty is a very worthy way of going," Trump told reporters outside the
White House before heading to Syracuse, New York, for the midterm election campaign.
When reporters asked whether he would watch the execution, Trump described Hasan as one of the worst killers."He's one of the worst killers. He walked into a room; he started killing everybody," Trump said.
The remarks come after US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said the execution would be carried out by a firing squad of soldiers at Fort Hood on December 3 at 1 pm, the same time the 2009 attack took place.
Speaking to Real America's Voice on Thursday (local time), Hegseth described the decision as a "no-brainer" and said the execution would be held at the military installation where Hasan carried out the attack.
"No-brainer. Execution by firing squad. Army major betrays his country, radical Islamist kills a bunch of Americans at Fort Hood. Of course we're going to do it at Fort Hood. We're going to do it on a Thursday. We're going to do it at 1:00, which is when he did it. And it's going to be soldiers with rifles executing the firing squad," Hegseth said.
He also said the execution would be made public so people could understand the consequences of such attacks.
"We haven't done this since WWII…He's going to get a firing squad of soldiers, as it should be. And we'll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it's public because people need to understand that what this is, there's serious consequences for these types of things," Hegseth said.
According to Axios, the US has not held a public execution in 90 years. The Pentagon says the execution will be livestreamed but did not name the platform, Axios reported.
The Department of Defence declined to comment on Hegseth’s remarks, and it remains unclear whether the execution will be open to spectators, broadcast, or shown to select individuals.

“Sounds that may have been mistaken for gunfire came from flashbang devices — chemical munitions — used by SWAT officers,” he said.
Gov. Josh Shapiro said he offered his administration’s “full support” to Erie Mayor Daria Devlin, who spoke directly to the victims’ families during the news conference.
“I am so deeply sorry. What happened to you was horrific, and there is nothing that any of us can say today that will make this any easier,” she said. “But you do need to know that our entire community is with you, we’re grieving with you. And we are here to support you.”
District Attorney Elizabeth Hirz urged the public to refrain from speculation as the investigation continues.
“Please do not allow rumors, speculation or unverified information to add to the pain that these families are already experiencing,” she said.

sources.news_title: Nine dead after mass shooting in Pennsylvania
sources.text:
‘It was horrific’: Eight people from same family killed in US shooting
Updated ,first published
Warning graphic content
Eight people from the same family, including a five-year-old boy, a one-year-old girl, and a woman who was eight months pregnant, have been killed in a shooting in Erie, Pennsylvania, police said, in one of the worst mass shootings in the city’s history.
A doorbell camera captured two women frantically trying to catch the attention of neighbours to raise the alarm about what was happening inside the house. Moments later, the two women, a relative and a family friend, were also shot dead in the street.
Police said the shooter died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound and there was no ongoing threat to public safety.
All the deaths occurred before officers arrived at the scene, where they were met with an eerie silence, the city’s police chief Rick Lorah said at a press conference on Sunday morning AEDT.
“There was no movement, no audible sounds coming from inside the residence, no gunshots, no screams,” he said.
“It was horrific. It was the worst scene I have ever experienced.
“Out of respect for the victims and the families, I will not discuss the details of what our officers encountered inside that home. But I want our community to understand the gravity of what happened and the profound impact this tragedy has had on those involved and on our community as a whole.”
Jennifer Lott, who lives on the block where the shooting took place, said she was at home when she heard gunshots and a woman lying in the street.
“I got closer, and I noticed she had a gunshot wound to her head and she wasn’t moving, and everybody kept telling me to back up; the police were coming,” she told The New York Times on Saturday.
Lorah said police had received doorbell video and audio from a home next door, including a scream and two muffled gunshots.
“That is where we were able to see those two females pacing back and forth outside the residence; they were trying to get neighbours’ attention,” he said.
“Video evidence reviewed by investigators shows those two women arriving at the residence appearing distressed, seeking assistance from neighbours and pounding on the door. The audio video also appears to capture muffled gunfire from inside the residence before the suspect emerged and fatally shot both women.”
Inside the home, two young children were found on the first floor: a five-year-old boy and a one-year-old girl. Four additional victims were found on the second floor in the stairwell: a 24-year-old female, a 44-year-old female, a 19-year-old male, and a 21-year-old male. The 45-year-old suspected shooter was found dead on the second floor from an apparent self-inflicted gunshot wound.
Lorah said he had been a police officer for 28 years and that he had never “seen the loss of life and the devastation that we just witnessed.”
“This is one of the most difficult and heartbreaking scenes our officers and investigators have ever encountered,” Lorah said. “The loss of life is devastating, and the circumstances we are working through are deeply disturbing.”
Governor Josh Shapiro said Saturday he offered his administration’s “full support” to Erie Mayor Daria Devlin.
“I’ve spoken with Mayor Devlin and offered my Administration’s full support following the tragic mass shooting in Erie last night — killing nine of our fellow Pennsylvanians,” Shapiro wrote in a Saturday morning post on X.
Erie is the fifth most populous city in Pennsylvania and is located on the shores of Lake Erie.
Watch: Erie Police chief Rick Lorah’s press conference on Sunday morning AEDT.

‘Deeply disturbing’: 9 dead in Pennsylvania shooting, police chief says
sources.text:
‘Deeply disturbing’: 9 dead in Pennsylvania shooting, police chief says
ERIE, Pa. (WICU/WSEE) — Nine people are dead after a shooting Friday night, authorities said.
Police said the suspected shooter died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound.
Witnesses said the suspect was seen firing a weapon before entering a house.
Police respond to scene
Police arrived at the scene near 7th and Perry streets, and tried to get the man to surrender. Additional gunshots were then heard from inside the home.
“At this time we can confirm that the suspect is deceased. Based on the information currently available to us, there is no ongoing threat to the public,” Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah said.
There is no word yet on a possible motive. The identities of the victims have not been released.
“I want to be candid with our community. This is one of the most difficult and heartbreaking scenes our officers and investigators have ever encountered. The loss of life is devastating, and the circumstances we are working through are deeply disturbing,” Lorah said.
An investigation into the matter is ongoing.
